groups.label: Identity & Record
groups.description: Stable internal keys, slug, record tier, primary common name, and the canonical accepted scientific name. The minimal anchor every taxon carries.

groups.label: Naming & Nomenclature
groups.description: Authorship, basionym, synonymy, homonymy, type specimen, nomenclatural acts, registration, and etymology. Owns the ICN naming layer.

groups.label: Classification & Phylogeny
groups.description: Ranked classification path (kingdom→infraspecific), parent linkage, species complex, molecular phylogenetic placement, sister taxa, and reclassification history.

groups.label: Macroscopic Morphology
groups.description: Naked-eye basidiome/ascoma features: cap, hymenophore, stipe, veils, flesh, latex, spore print, sensory, bruising, development. Genus-dependent and nullable.

groups.label: Microscopy & Anatomy
groups.description: Spores (dimensions, Q, ornamentation, reactions), basidia, cystidia, hyphal system, tissue layers, asci/ascospores, crystals, and measurement-protocol metadata.

groups.label: Chemistry, Toxins & Medicinal
groups.description: Toxin inventory and toxidromes, psychoactive and medicinal compounds, nutrition, bioaccumulation, allergens, pigments, and macrochemical spot tests. Owns compound identity and hazard axis.

groups.label: Edibility & Safety
groups.description: Safety-first edibility classification, preparation requirements, dangerous lookalikes, sensory/culinary profile, preservation, and consumption cautions. The actionable safety layer.

groups.label: Ecology & Habitat
groups.description: Trophic mode, substrate/host associations, habitat/biome, climate/soil preference, fruiting phenology, ecological role, and conservation status.

groups.label: Distribution & Biogeography
groups.description: Native/introduced range, country/region distribution, biogeographic realms, elevation, occurrence-record statistics, and range dynamics.

groups.label: Cultivation & Lab
groups.description: Cultivability, substrate recipes, environmental parameter ranges by phase, lifecycle timelines, yield, contamination, senescence, strains, and commercial positioning.

groups.label: Genetics & Molecular
groups.description: DNA barcodes/markers, genome assemblies, karyology, mating systems, ex-type sequences, intraspecific variation, and toxin/psilocybin biosynthesis gene clusters.

groups.label: Ethnomycology & History
groups.description: Multilingual vernacular names with provenance, discovery history, folklore, traditional/ritual use, cultural significance, and references in art and media.

groups.label: Media
groups.description: Images, microscopy, audio, video, and 3D assets — each independently licensed and credited, with view type, lifecycle stage, and ID verification status.

groups.label: Provenance & Data Quality
groups.description: Cross-cutting per-field source/confidence/verification model, citations, external authority links, record licensing, completeness/quality scoring, contributors, and dispute flags.

fields.label: Record ID
fields.notes: Stable internal primary key for the taxon concept; survives renames. Merges acceptedNameId + recordId from source domains.

fields.label: URL Slug
fields.notes: Lowercase hyphenated; stable URL component and shard key (first letter).

fields.label: Record Curation Tier
fields.notes: Drives static pre-render vs client-fetch fallback (CLAUDE.md §3). stub/imported → client; curated/featured → pre-rendered.

fields.label: Scientific Name (with authorship)
fields.notes: Canonical accepted name WITH authorship. Identity anchor for all safety records.

fields.label: Canonical Name (no authorship)
fields.notes: Name string without authorship for search, joins, and display.

fields.label: Primary Common Name
fields.notes: Single canonical English vernacular for display. Full multilingual set with provenance lives in culture.vernacularNames.

fields.label: Taxonomic Rank
fields.notes: Rank of THIS record. Historical division/subdivision map to phylum/subphylum.

fields.label: Taxonomic Status
fields.notes: Accepted vs synonym/misapplied. A toxic species may be searched under a synonym.

fields.label: Accepted Name Usage ID
fields.notes: If this record is a synonym, points to the accepted taxon recordId so synonym searches reach the correct (possibly toxic) species.

fields.label: Full Authorship String
fields.notes: Complete authority including parentheses, ex-author, combining author.

fields.label: Basionym Authorship
fields.notes: Parenthetical author(s) of the basionym.

fields.label: Combination Authorship
fields.notes: Author of the current combination (outside parentheses).

fields.label: Year of Publication
fields.notes: Year the accepted name was validly published.

fields.label: Governing Nomenclatural Code
fields.notes: Fungi default to ICN; environmental dark-taxa may use UNITE SH / provisional.

fields.label: Nomenclatural Status
fields.notes: ICN name-level standing, orthogonal to taxonomic acceptance.

fields.label: Sanctioning Status
fields.notes: Fries/Persoon sanctioning confers priority under ICN Art. F.7.

fields.label: Basionym
fields.notes: Original name on which the current combination is based.

fields.label: Synonyms
fields.notes: Each {name, authorship, synonymType, registryId, year}. Searches under any synonym must resolve to the accepted toxic taxon.

fields.label: Misapplied Names
fields.notes: Names erroneously applied in literature; major source of ID/poisoning confusion.

fields.label: Orthographic Variants
fields.notes: Spelling variants/corrigenda to aid matching.

fields.label: Type Specimen Status
fields.notes: Kind of name-bearing type. Epitype heavily used in fungi for DNA reference.

fields.label: Type Specimen Citation
fields.notes: Free-text citation of the type as published.

fields.label: Type Herbarium (Index Herbariorum)
fields.notes: Index Herbariorum acronym holding the type. Physical specimen lives in provenance.

fields.label: Type Locality
fields.notes: Place where the name-bearing type was collected. Coordinates belong to distribution.

fields.label: Protologue Citation
fields.notes: Bibliographic citation of the original description.

fields.label: Etymology
fields.example: phalloides = 'phallus-like', from the young button's resemblance
fields.notes: Derivation/meaning of the epithet (and genus where notable).

fields.label: Etymology Root Language
fields.notes: Source of the epithet's derivation.

fields.label: Anamorph/Teleomorph Link
fields.notes: Pre-2011 dual nomenclature linkage; under 1F1N track the suppressed name. Toxin producers often known under the anamorph.

fields.label: Phylum
fields.notes: Canonical higher-rank home; molecular phylum placement de-duped here.

fields.label: Infraspecific Epithet
fields.notes: Epithet for subspecies/variety/form.

fields.label: Intermediate Ranks
fields.notes: Sparse map of any populated intermediate/infrageneric ranks (subkingdom, subphylum, subclass, superorder, suborder, subfamily, tribe, subgenus, section, series). Keeps the core flat while allowing depth.

fields.label: Materialized Classification Path
fields.notes: Ordered rank→name pairs for breadcrumbs and ancestor queries.

fields.label: Parent Taxon ID
fields.notes: Direct parent recordId; enables tree assembly.

fields.label: Species Complex / Aggregate
fields.notes: Cryptic-species grouping. Matters when toxicity differs across cryptic members.

fields.label: Part of Cryptic Species Group
fields.notes: Morphologically similar but genetically distinct species confused under this name.

fields.label: Phylogenetic Clade
fields.notes: Finest-resolution molecular clade/section.

fields.label: Sister Taxa / Nearest Relatives
fields.notes: Closest relatives by molecular phylogeny; lookalike/safety context.

fields.label: Classification Confidence
fields.notes: How settled the placement/acceptance is.

fields.label: Recent Reclassification Note
fields.notes: Genus transfers/splits that change which safety profile a name maps to.

fields.label: Sporocarp Type
fields.notes: Gross form; gates which downstream morphology fields apply.

fields.label: Cap Shape
fields.notes: Profile(s) across maturity.

fields.label: Cap Color (Primary)
fields.notes: Pair with colorChartCode free-text via provenance for precise hue.

fields.label: Cap Ornamentation
fields.notes: Distinguishes Amanita warts vs Lepiota scales.

fields.label: Hymenophore Type
fields.notes: Gates gill vs pore vs tooth subfields.

fields.label: Gill Attachment
fields.notes: Free gills + volva => Amanita.

fields.label: Gill Color
fields.notes: Often tracks spore color; Agaricus pink→brown vs Amanita white.

fields.label: Pore Surface Color
fields.notes: Red pores + blue staining is a caution flag (boletes).

fields.label: Pore Density
fields.notes: Polypore character; null for non-poroid taxa.

fields.label: Hydnoid Tooth Length
fields.notes: Hydnoid taxa only.

fields.label: Stipe Dimensions
fields.notes: {length:range, width:range}.

fields.label: Annulus (Ring) Present
fields.notes: Critical safety character (Amanita/Lepiota have rings).

fields.label: Cortina Present
fields.notes: Defines Cortinarius (orellanine genus).

fields.label: Volva (Universal Veil Cup) Present
fields.notes: THE key Amanita safety character — presence demands extreme caution.

fields.label: Stipe Base Form
fields.notes: Marginate/abrupt bulb is an Amanita warning sign.

fields.label: Basal Mycelium / Rhizomorphs
fields.notes: Black bootlace rhizomorphs typify Armillaria.

fields.label: Flesh Color Change on Cutting
fields.notes: Oxidation change after sectioning; major bolete safety character.

fields.label: Latex Present
fields.notes: Defines Lactarius/Lactifluus.

fields.label: Latex Color Change on Exposure
fields.notes: Major Lactarius diagnostic.

fields.label: Spore Print Color
fields.notes: Foundational ID/keying character and safety discriminator (white-spored Amanita). Microscopy owns the chart-coded variant.

fields.label: Odor Descriptor
fields.notes: Phenolic flags toxic Agaricus; fetid flags Phallaceae.

fields.label: Taste Descriptor
fields.notes: Chew-and-spit only. Acrid/bitter signals inedibility. Never swallow; never taste suspected Amanita/Cortinarius.

fields.label: General Bruising / Staining
fields.notes: {description, color(enumRef BruisingColor), speed(enumRef BruisingSpeed)}. Bluing => possible psilocybin.

fields.label: Gleba Description (Gasteroid)
fields.notes: Cut-young-white test distinguishes puffballs from Amanita eggs.

fields.label: Autodigestion / Deliquescence
fields.notes: Inky dissolution at maturity (Coprinus s.l.); coprine context.

fields.label: Basidiome Development Type
fields.notes: Reijnders/Kuhner ontogeny terminology; expert veil-interpretation character.

fields.label: Overall Consistency
fields.notes: Separates soft agarics from woody polypores.

fields.label: Basidiospore Dimensions
fields.notes: {length:range, width:range, lengthMean?, widthMean?, extremesNote?}. Apiculus/ornamentation excluded unless protocol notes otherwise.

fields.label: Q Ratio (length/width)
fields.notes: {range, mean?}. Shape descriptor (Q≈1 globose).

fields.label: Spore Reaction in Melzer's
fields.notes: Amyloid spores in Amanita sect. Phalloideae are part of toxic-species ID.

fields.label: Germ Pore
fields.notes: Distinct apical pore diagnostic for psychoactive dark-spored genera (Psilocybe, Panaeolus).

fields.label: Sterigmata per Basidium
fields.notes: 2- vs 4-spored affects spore size/ploidy.

fields.label: Cheilocystidia
fields.notes: {presence(enumRef CystidiaPresence), shapes(array enumRef CystidiaShape), size, wallType?}. Gill-edge cystidia; primary species character.

fields.label: Pleurocystidia
fields.notes: Same shape as cheilocystidia. Metuloids diagnostic in Inocybe/Pluteus.

fields.label: Hyphal System
fields.notes: Central to polypore taxonomy.

fields.label: Clamp Connections
fields.notes: Core genus-level character.

fields.label: Lamellar Trama Type
fields.notes: Bilateral trama (Amanita, Pluteus); with-sphaerocytes defines Russulales.

fields.label: Pileipellis Type
fields.notes: Correlates with cap viscidity (macro). ixo- = gelatinized.

fields.label: Setae / Setal Hyphae
fields.notes: Dark pointed setae define Hymenochaetaceae.

fields.label: Crystals in Tissue
fields.notes: Acanthocytes diagnostic for Stropharia; calcium oxalate dissolves in KOH.

fields.label: Ascus Type (Ascomycota)
fields.notes: Operculate (Pezizales) vs inoperculate fundamental for ascomycetes.

fields.label: Ascospore Features (Ascomycota)
fields.notes: {shape, size, ornamentation}. Muriform/reticulate diagnostic in Morchella/Tuber.

fields.label: Measurement Protocol Metadata
fields.notes: {mountingMedium(enumRef MountingMedium), magnification?, n?, numberCollections?, fromTissue?, ornamentationIncluded?, apiculusIncluded?, extremesConvention?, observer?, voucherSpecimenId?}. Mandatory context for reproducible micro-measurements; medium changes measured size.

fields.label: Overall Toxicity Class
fields.notes: Hazard axis, orthogonal to culinary edibility.
fields.sourceHint: toxicology literature / NAMA / clinical case series

fields.label: Secondary Toxidromes
fields.notes: Many amatoxin species also cause early GI symptoms.

fields.label: Symptom Onset Category
fields.notes: Delayed onset (>6h) is the danger flag (amatoxin/gyromitrin/orellanine).

fields.label: Toxin Inventory
fields.notes: Per-toxin nested objects. CID/CAS realistic placeholders if unverified.

fields.label: Estimated Human Lethal Dose
fields.example: ~0.1 mg amatoxin/kg; ~50 g fresh A. phalloides can be fatal
fields.notes: Free-text: mixes mg toxin/kg and fresh tissue mass.

fields.label: Antidotes / Treatments
fields.notes: Educational only; UI must surface a medical-caution Aside.

fields.label: Toxin Cooking Stability
fields.notes: Amatoxins heat_stable; informs edibility prep validity.

fields.label: Psychoactive Compound Profile
fields.notes: Per-compound name, percentDryWt range, pubchemCid. psilocybin/psilocin/baeocystin/muscimol/ibotenic_acid.

fields.label: Medicinal / Bioactive Inventory
fields.notes: Per-compound name, compoundClass(enumRef MedicinalCompoundClass), concentration, claimedActivity, evidenceGrade.

fields.label: Medicinal Claim Evidence Grade
fields.notes: Anti-overclaim gate.

fields.label: Nutritional Composition (per 100g)
fields.notes: Owned here; Edibility references via provenance. {basis, kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbohydrate_g, fiber_g, water_g, ash_g}.

fields.label: Known Bioaccumulator
fields.notes: Quick wild-harvest safety flag even when edible.

fields.label: Heavy Metal / Radionuclide Profile
fields.notes: Per-element {element(enumRef BioaccumElement), concentration:range, bioconcentrationFactor, notes}.

fields.label: Bluing / Oxidation Staining
fields.notes: Bluing in Psilocybe = presumptive psilocin; in boletes = variegatic acid (unrelated).

fields.label: Macrochemical Spot Tests
fields.notes: Per-test {reagent(enumRef MacrochemicalReagent), tissue, result}. Schaeffer cross-reaction separates edible from toxic Agaricus.

fields.label: Pigment Chemistry
fields.notes: Per-pigment {name, pigmentClass(enumRef PigmentClass), color, role}. Underlies bluing/staining.

fields.label: Controlled-Substance Status
fields.notes: Coarse flag; jurisdiction detail in notes.

fields.label: Edibility Classification
fields.notes: Single authoritative classification; pick the most conservative applicable value. Replaces legacy free-text edibility enum.
fields.sourceHint: primary literature / regional field guides / NAMA; never auto-classify

fields.label: Edibility Confidence
fields.notes: Drives whether a caution Aside is surfaced.

fields.label: Novice-Safety Rating
fields.notes: Forager-skill gate factoring lookalike danger.

fields.label: Deadly Lookalike Risk Level
fields.notes: Summary flag; detail in dangerousLookalikes.

fields.label: Toxic / Irritant When Raw
fields.notes: Note: A. phalloides is deadly cooked OR raw; this flag is for species edible only when cooked.

fields.label: Mandatory Preparation
fields.notes: Ordered {step(enumRef PreparationStep), detail, removesHazard}. Validity gated by chemistry.toxinThermolability.

fields.label: Alcohol Interaction (Coprine-type)
fields.notes: Coprine reaction window up to ~72h.

fields.label: Dangerous Lookalikes
fields.example: [{species:'Volvariella speciosa',toxicity:'edible',confusionDirection:'this_mistaken_for_edible',distinguishingFeatures:['white spore print vs pink','presence of ring'],confusionLikelihood:'moderate'}]
fields.notes: Per-lookalike {species, toxicity(enumRef EdibilityClass), confusionDirection(enumRef ConfusionDirection), distinguishingFeatures, confusionLikelihood(enumRef LookalikeRiskLevel), region?}.

fields.label: Key Disambiguation Tests
fields.example: ["Spore print color (white)","Excavate base to check for volva","Amyloid spores in Melzer's"]

fields.label: Idiosyncratic Reaction Risk
fields.notes: Otherwise-edible species causing reactions in some individuals.

fields.label: Culinary Taste Rating
fields.notes: Gastronomic quality, separate from safety.

fields.label: Aroma / Odor Descriptors
fields.notes: Some double as toxicity signals; sensory-primary.

fields.label: Regional / Chemotype Variation
fields.example: Uniformly deadly across its range; no safe regional chemotype

fields.label: Special-Population Caution
fields.notes: Children, pregnancy, immunocompromised advisories.

fields.label: Primary Trophic Mode
fields.notes: Canonical owner; gates cultivability. FungalTraits/FUNGuild aligned.

fields.label: Substrate Type(s)
fields.notes: Wild substrate. Lab/induced substrate lives in cultivation.

fields.label: Host / Plant Associations
fields.notes: {taxon, rank, relationship(enumRef HostRelationship), specificity(enumRef HostSpecificity)}. Critical foraging ID cue.

fields.label: Host Breadth (Angio/Gymno)
fields.notes: Hardwood vs conifer matters for ID and lookalike separation.

fields.label: Soil Type Preference
fields.notes: Wild edaphic preference. Cultivation substrate pH is separate.

fields.label: Fruiting Season(s)
fields.notes: Hemisphere-normalized; pair with phenologyHemisphere. Top foraging cue.

fields.label: Fruiting Triggers
fields.notes: Wild cues. Lab induction in cultivation.

fields.label: Fruiting Body Position
fields.notes: Truffles hypogeous; affects detection.

fields.label: Abundance / Commonness
fields.notes: Region-scope via provenance/abundanceByRegion where needed.

fields.label: Legal Protection / Harvest Restriction
fields.notes: {jurisdiction, protection}. Some countries restrict harvesting.

fields.label: Habitat & Ecology Notes
fields.example: Mycorrhizal with oak and other hardwoods, occasionally conifers; widely naturalized with planted hosts.
fields.notes: Replaces legacy free-text habitat field.

fields.label: Native Range (description)
fields.example: Native to Europe; introduced widely with exotic hosts

fields.label: Country Distribution
fields.notes: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of countries with verified records.

fields.label: Introduced Range
fields.notes: ISO codes where introduced/naturalized (often with exotic hosts).

fields.label: Occurrence Centroid
fields.notes: Mean lat/lon for range maps and climate matching.

fields.label: GBIF Occurrence Count
fields.notes: Documentation richness proxy, not true abundance. Sync timestamp via provenance.

fields.label: iNaturalist Observation Count
fields.notes: Encounter/photograph frequency proxy; feeds MycoGram image pool.

fields.label: Range Shift / Expansion Notes
fields.example: Established and spreading in North America with introduced oaks and other hosts.

fields.label: Cultivable
fields.notes: Ectomycorrhizal species generally cannot be fruited indoors.

fields.label: Lab Fruiting Temp Range
fields.notes: Lab/induced; wild fruiting temp lives in ecology.

fields.label: Senescence / Degradation Susceptibility
fields.notes: Differentiator content area for MycoSci gene-science pillar.

fields.label: Long-Term Culture Storage
fields.notes: Cryo is gold standard to arrest senescence.

fields.label: Forms Sclerotia
fields.notes: Psilocybe 'truffles', Wolfiporia. Alternate cultivation product.

fields.label: Recommended Strains / Cultivars
fields.notes: {name, traits}. For psychoactive species, strain list is safety-relevant.

fields.label: Cultivation Legal Status Note
fields.notes: Flag where growing (esp. psychoactive) is legally controlled.

fields.label: Mating System
fields.notes: Self-compatibility; affects breeding/cultivation. Canonical owner (cultivation references).

fields.label: Ploidy
fields.notes: Basidiomycota vegetative phase typically dikaryotic.

fields.label: Chromosome Count (n)
fields.notes: From PFGE or genome assembly.

fields.label: ITS Barcode
fields.notes: {available, accessions[], lengthBp?, refSequenceUrl?}. ITS = formal fungal barcode. Accessions are realistic placeholders unless verified.

fields.label: UNITE Species Hypothesis (SH)
fields.notes: DOI-backed SH clustering ITS at a threshold; critical for dark taxa.

fields.label: Other Phylogenetic Markers
fields.notes: {marker(enumRef GeneticMarker), accessions[]}. LSU/SSU/RPB2/TEF1/TUB2 etc. Accession provenance; biology described here.

fields.label: Recommended ID Marker
fields.notes: Best-practice marker(s) for confident ID in this lineage.

fields.label: Ex-Type Sequence Available
fields.notes: {available, accessions:[{marker, accession, typeStatus(enumRef TypeStatus)}]}. Highest molecular-ID provenance tier.

fields.label: Genome Assembly
fields.notes: {sequenced, assemblyAccessions[], sizeMb:range?, gcContent?, geneCount?, assemblyLevel(enumRef AssemblyLevel)?, buscoCompleteness?}.
fields.sourceHint: NCBI Assembly / JGI MycoCosm / Ensembl Fungi

fields.label: Population Structure / Phylogeography
fields.example: European source populations; introduced North American lineages from multiple events.

fields.label: Toxin Biosynthesis Gene Clusters
fields.notes: Molecular basis of toxicity: amatoxin MSDIN+POPB, aflatoxin PKS, etc.

fields.label: Psilocybin Biosynthesis Genes
fields.notes: {present, genes[]} psiD/psiK/psiM/psiH. Molecular marker of psychoactivity.

fields.label: Known Only From Environmental Sequences
fields.notes: 'Dark taxon' flag; relevant for SH-based provisional names.

fields.label: Vernacular Names
fields.notes: {name, langCode, regionCode?, script?, isPrimary?, usageStatus(enumRef NameUsageStatus), transliteration?, ipa?, source?}. Owns the provenanced multilingual set; identity.primaryCommonName denormalizes the English preferred.
fields.sourceHint: GBIF vernaculars / iNaturalist / Wikidata / ethnobotanical literature

fields.label: Indigenous / First-Nations Names
fields.notes: {name, culture, langCode, glossMeaning, source}. Handle with cultural sensitivity; see culturalSensitivityFlag.
fields.sourceHint: ethnomycological / linguistic field studies with attribution

fields.label: Original Describer(s)
fields.example: [{name:'Elias Magnus Fries',role:'sanctioning author',year:1821},{name:'Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link',role:'combining author',year:1833}]
fields.notes: Human-readable describers with role; links to historicalFigures.
fields.sourceHint: protologue / Index Fungorum / Harvard Index of Botanists

fields.label: Discovery & Description History
fields.example: Long recognized in European folk culture as deadly before formal description; the section Phalloideae is the most lethal in Amanita.

fields.label: Associated Historical Figures
fields.notes: {name, role, contribution, era}.

fields.label: Folklore & Mythology
fields.notes: {tradition, motif, summary, region}.

fields.label: Traditional / Ethnographic Uses
fields.notes: {useType(enumRef UseType), culture, description, era, evidenceLevel?}. Ritual/medicinal/edible uses are safety-relevant — never read as endorsement.

fields.label: Notable Poisonings / Historical Cases
fields.example: [{caseName:'Pope Clement VII (disputed)',year:1534,summary:'Death attributed by some accounts to Amanita phalloides; historically disputed',outcome:'fatal',verified:false}]
fields.notes: {caseName, year, summary, victims?, outcome(enumRef PoisoningOutcome), verified, references?}. Owns historical/anecdotal framing; chemistry owns mechanism.
fields.sourceHint: medical case reports / historical records / poison-control archives

fields.label: References in Art, Literature & Media
fields.notes: {work, author, year, mediaType(enumRef MediaReferenceType), context}. Includes art, literature, film, games, stamps.

fields.label: Cultural Significance
fields.example: The archetypal deadly mushroom; the single most lethal fungus to humans worldwide, responsible for the majority of fatal mushroom poisonings.

fields.label: Popular Misconceptions / Debunked Lore
fields.example: [{claim:'Cooking or drying renders it safe',status:'dangerous false belief',correction:'Amatoxins are heat-stable; no preparation makes it safe'}]
fields.notes: {claim, status, correction}. Critical for an authoritative dataset.

fields.label: Cultural Sensitivity Flag
fields.notes: Marks Indigenous/sacred/restricted knowledge requiring careful attribution.

fields.label: Media Assets
fields.notes: Array of independently-licensed assets. See MediaAsset interface. A misID'd image is a safety hazard. Default license 'unknown' blocks redistribution.

fields.label: Primary Image Reference
fields.notes: FK into media[] for the hero image; denormalized for fast card/feed render.

fields.label: Has Microscopy Media
fields.notes: Facet flag for deep-search index.

fields.label: Per-Field Provenance
fields.notes: THE cross-cutting structure: attaches {field(path), sourceRefId, sourceType(enumRef SourceType), confidence(enumRef ConfidenceLevel), verificationStatus(enumRef FieldVerificationStatus), verifiedBy?, reviewedOn?, note?} to any field in any group. Sparse: only present for asserted fields, not every field. ai-generated-unverified flagged distinctly.

fields.label: Citations & References
fields.notes: Bibliography backing the record. {refId, type(enumRef ReferenceType), doi?, url?, title, authors?, year?, containerTitle?, pages?, isbn?, isPrimary?}. fieldProvenance cites these by refId.

fields.label: External Authority Links
fields.notes: Canonical cross-references; identity resolution depends on them. {authority(enumRef ExternalAuthority), externalId, url?, relationship(enumRef LinkRelationship)?, lastSynced?}. De-duped from per-domain identifier fields.
fields.sourceHint: MycoBank / Index Fungorum / GBIF / NCBI / iNaturalist / Wikidata

fields.label: Data Completeness Score
fields.notes: Tier-weighted fraction of expected fields populated; drives curation prompts.

fields.label: Record Verification Level
fields.notes: Record-level trust badge; gates how strongly edibility claims are presented.

fields.label: Contributors
fields.notes: {handle, role(enumRef ContributorRole), contributedOn?}. Supports attribution and leaderboard.

fields.notes: {field, reason, status(enumRef DisputeStatus), raisedBy?}. Safety-relevant on edibility; surfaces a caution banner until resolved.

fields.notes: License of the MycoSci record itself, DISTINCT from per-asset media licenses. The 'open' guarantee.

fields.notes: For migration safety as stubs enrich.

designNotes:
TIERING. Three tiers let ~24k stubs enrich without schema churn. CORE = identity + safety only: recordId, slug, recordTier, scientificName, canonicalName, primaryCommonName, taxonRank, taxonomicStatus, acceptedNameUsageId, the seven Linnaean rank strings (kingdom..specificEpithet), parentNameUsageId, plus the safety triad edibilityClass/edibilityConfidence/toxicityClass and the provenance backbone (fieldProvenance, references, externalLinks, verificationLevel, recordLicense). A stub is a valid record carrying only core fields. STANDARD = a good profile (key morphology, ecology, distribution, common sensory/safety). DEEP = expert/rare (microscopy protocol metadata, gene clusters, development ontogeny, folklore detail). Every field is optional except the core identity keys, so a stub and a reference-quality record share one schema/one TS type; enrichment is additive. recordTier is the promotion flag from CLAUDE.md §3: stub/imported render client-side from sharded JSON; curated/featured/reference-quality pre-render via getStaticPaths. No code change to promote — flip recordTier and add fields.

DE-DUPLICATION DECISIONS. (1) Common names: the provenanced multilingual set lives once in culture.vernacularNames; identity.primaryCommonName is a denormalized English display string (fast cards/search) flagged as derived. (2) Identifiers: all external DB IDs (MycoBank, IndexFungorum, GBIF, NCBI, iNaturalist, Wikidata, UNITE, BOLD, etc.) collapse into one provenance.externalLinks[] array — taxonomy/ecology/genetics no longer each carry their own ID fields. The only molecular IDs kept in genetics are sequence/assembly accessions (itsBarcode, otherMarkers, exTypeSequence, genome), because those are sequence records, not taxon-concept IDs. (3) Spore-print color: macroscopic field color owned by morphology.sporePrintColor; microscopy keeps only the chart-coded/individual-spore reactions. (4) Trophic mode: canonical owner ecology.trophicMode; cultivation reads it for cultivability gating (cultivation.cultivable) rather than re-storing it. (5) Toxin identity owned by chemistry.toxins[]; edibility carries only the actionable classification + rationale and cross-references via fieldProvenance. (6) Mating system canonical in genetics; cultivation references it. (7) Phylum: one classification.phylum (molecular placement folded in). (8) Nutrition raw composition owned by chemistry; edibility references. (9) Spot-test reagent vocab (MacrochemicalReagent) shared by chemistry + microscopy as one enum.

PROVENANCE / CONFIDENCE MODEL. Rather than bloat every field with source/confidence wrappers, provenance is a single sparse array fieldProvenance[] keyed by dotted field path. Only asserted, non-trivial, or safety-relevant fields get an entry; the rest inherit the record-level verificationLevel. Each entry carries sourceRefId (FK into references[] or externalLinks), sourceType, confidence, verificationStatus, verifiedBy, reviewedOn, and an optional note. This makes per-claim citation badges and 'low/disputed' caution banners possible without doubling the field count, and keeps stub JSON tiny (a stub may have zero or one provenance entries). SourceType deliberately includes ai-generated-unverified and machine-inference as distinct flags so the anti-fabrication policy (CLAUDE.md §9) is enforceable in data: any field whose only provenance is ai-generated-unverified must not be presented as fact, and safety fields (edibility/toxicity) require a primary-literature/peer-reviewed/authority-database source before verificationLevel can exceed community-reviewed.

UNITS & RANGES. All quantitative values use a NumericRange {min, max, unit} object; a single value sets min === max. Dimensionless values (Q ratio) use unit ''. Composite measurements nest ranges (stipeDimensions.length/width, basidiosporeDimensions). Units are stored explicitly per value (never implied globally) so mm/µm/°C/%RH/ppm/mg-g/Mb coexist safely and a UI can convert. Enums are centralized once (enums[]) and referenced by enumRef; multi-valued descriptive fields (capColor, odor, cystidia shapes) are arrays of the enum because real taxa span several values. Genus-dependence is handled by making nearly everything nullable plus 'not-applicable' enum members — a polypore simply omits gill fields; an ascomycete omits basidiospore fields and populates ascus fields.

STATIC-SITE FIT. The record is plain JSON with no runtime dependencies, ideal for sharded public/data/species/{first-letter}.json fetched client-side for the long tail, and for getStaticPaths pre-render of curated taxa. Core fields are small enough that a shard of thousands of stubs stays well under the ~200KB target; deep arrays (media, toxins, microscopy, provenance) only materialize on curated records, so build cost scales with curated content, not catalog size. Search-index builders read the same canonical record (Pagefind over pre-rendered curated pages; MiniSearch/Orama over the flat stub fields: canonicalName, vernacularNames, taxonomy path, edibilityClass, habitatType, trophicMode). Safety-relevant fields are explicitly flagged so the UI can always surface a caution Aside for toxic/psychoactive/disputed taxa and never auto-present an unsourced edibility claim. This schema replaces the legacy src/content.config.ts flat string fields (habitat/distribution become structured ecology/distribution groups; the 5-value edibility enum is superseded by EdibilityClass with the conservative-value rule).
